claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu coating has an FCC lattice in the baseline state.
The Cu substrate is single-crystalline and FCC.
The coating maintains an ordered lattice up to 600 K.
The coating maintains a stable dislocation density up to 600 K.
Rapid lattice disorder develops above approximately 900 K.
Dislocation density decreases significantly above approximately 900 K.
The fraction of HCP-classified atoms increases above approximately 900 K.
Dislocation density decreases at moderate temperatures up to 600 K.
The moderate-temperature reduction in dislocation density increases the elastic modulus.
Above 900 K, lattice softening and disorder shift deformation from controlled stacking faults to widespread lattice disorder.
High-temperature lattice disorder alters the stress distribution during sliding.
The altered stress distribution increases tangential force during sliding.
The increased tangential force produces a higher friction coefficient above 900 K.
Hardness remains relatively stable from 300 K through 600 K.
Wear resistance remains relatively stable from 300 K through 600 K.
Hardness decreases sharply above approximately 900 K.
Elastic modulus decreases sharply above approximately 900 K.
Wear resistance decreases sharply above approximately 900 K as elastic modulus drops.
Friction coefficient increases significantly above approximately 900 K because of enhanced lattice disorder.
Higher baseline dislocation density causes higher hardness and wear resistance and lower friction at 300 K.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator says dislocation density remains stable up to 600 K, whereas the mechanism says dislocation density decreases over that same moderate-temperature range.

The mechanism treats reduced dislocation density as beneficial to elastic modulus up to 600 K, while the baseline attributes superior mechanical and tribological performance to higher dislocation density. The distinct outcome variables prevent a strict logical contradiction, but the proposed role of dislocation density is internally inconsistent and unexplained.
